name: District of Columbia
headline_status: Adults 21+ may possess and grow cannabis, but adult-use sales are blocked by Congress; only licensed medical sales are legal.
summary: District of Columbia voters approved Initiative 71 in November 2014, and since February 2015 adults 21+ may possess up to two ounces, grow a few plants at home and give away up to one ounce. A congressional budget rider in place since 2014 bars the District from taxing and regulating adult-use sales, so the only legal stores are licensed medical dispensaries. Since a 2022 law, adults 21+ can self-certify as medical patients without a doctor's recommendation, and since mid-2024 regulators have used new powers to close unlicensed cannabis shops.

adult_use_since.value: Initiative 71 approved Nov. 4, 2014; took effect Feb. 26, 2015 after Congress's review period passed without action.

medical_since.value: Voters approved medical cannabis in 1998, but Congress blocked it from taking effect until 2009.

possession_limit.value: Adults 21+ may possess up to 2 ounces and give up to 1 ounce to another adult with no payment involved.

home_grow.value: Up to 6 plants, no more than 3 of them mature and flowering.

purchase_age.value: 21 and older to possess or grow; adults 21+ may self-certify to buy at medical dispensaries.

retail_sales.value: No legal adult-use sales: the congressional 'Harris rider,' renewed in the fiscal 2026 budget, bars DC from regulating and taxing them. Only licensed medical dispensaries may sell.

medical_program.value: Under the Medical Cannabis Amendment Act of 2022 (signed Jan. 31, 2023), residents 21+ can self-certify with no doctor or qualifying condition required. Non-residents can get temporary registration, and visitors may use their home-state medical ID.

taxes.value: Medical cannabis is taxed at 6%; the DC Council rejected a proposed increase to 10% on June 9, 2026.

regulator.value: Alcoholic Beverage and Cannabis Administration (ABCA) and the ABC Board.

unlicensed_shops.value: Since July 15, 2024, ABCA can padlock unlicensed cannabis shops, and the ABC Board can fine property owners $10,000 and require a remediation plan.

timeline.event: Voters approve medical cannabis; Congress blocks implementation until 2009
Initiative 71 takes effect: adult possession, home grow and gifting become legal
Medical Cannabis Amendment Act of 2022 signed, allowing adult self-certification
Emergency law gives ABCA power to close unlicensed cannabis shops
DC Council rejects raising the medical cannabis tax from 6% to 10%

faq.a: Yes for adults 21+ to possess up to two ounces and grow at home. Adult-use sales are not legal because Congress blocks DC from regulating them.

faq.q: Where can you buy weed legally in DC?
faq.a: Only at licensed medical dispensaries. Adults 21+ can self-certify as medical patients without a doctor's recommendation, and visitors can use their home-state medical ID or get temporary registration.

faq.q: Are DC weed gifting shops legal?
faq.a: Initiative 71 only allows giving up to one ounce with no payment. Since July 2024 regulators have been padlocking unlicensed cannabis shops and fining property owners.

faq.q: How many plants can you grow in DC?
faq.a: Up to six plants, with no more than three mature and flowering at a time.

faq.q: Why can't DC have recreational dispensaries?
faq.a: A congressional budget rider in place since 2014, and renewed in the fiscal 2026 budget, bars the District from taxing and regulating adult-use sales.
